name: Bongaon oral rehydration deployment
description: During the 1971 Bangladesh refugee crisis, health workers and relatives helped provide oral rehydration at Bongaon in India.

date.basis: Date applies to the stated documented event or archaeological context, not to a worldwide origin.

events.statement: During the 1971 Bangladesh refugee crisis, health workers and relatives helped provide oral rehydration at Bongaon in India.

evidence.locator: Historical account and Table 1, 2012 WHO journal reprint
evidence.supports: The authors report oral rehydration delivered in 1971 by teams with relatives and paramedical workers at Bongaon, India. Of 3,703 admitted to the whole centre, 135 died; care included oral and intravenous therapy as appropriate. These observational outcomes do not isolate an effect of oral therapy.

events.caveats: The observational centre totals include mixed care; severe cases could receive intravenous fluids. The findings do not estimate the treatment’s isolated causal effect.

links.statement: The Bongaon report cited the 1968 studies among the earlier clinical work informing its field deployment.
links.scope: Cited research background for the deployment; NLM also documents a 1968 exchange of findings with the Calcutta team. This is not exclusive attribution or proof of a single direct transmission route.
links.alternatives: The report also cites other earlier clinical experience.
links.caveats: The 1968 source record synthesizes several studies with differing modes of administration. NLM documents a 1968 exchange with the Calcutta team, but it does not establish that this alone caused deployment at Bongaon.
links.timing: Studies were published in 1968; the field deployment occurred in 1971.

evidence.locator: 2012 reprint pp. 105 and 111–112, introduction and references 6–7
evidence.supports: The report explicitly cites 1968 studies in its discussion of previous clinical experience relevant to the 1971 deployment.

evidence.locator: Johns Hopkins Center for Medical Research and Training
evidence.supports: The NLM exhibition reports that David Nalin shared findings with the Johns Hopkins team in Calcutta in summer 1968; it later describes Mahalanabis organizing teams at Bongaon in 1971. This documented exchange provides context, not proof that a single person or meeting caused the 1971 deployment.
